# Part II: Technical Foundations {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
Part II establishes the technical substrate for AI-assisted architecture, spanning stage-gated lifecycles, structured hardware representations, learned design methods, tool-connected environments, and formal feedback.
:::

## Part Objectives

- Structurally decouple transient candidate representations from version-controlled, machine-usable project state.
- Evaluate learned optimization methods against physical design and HLS pragma space trade-offs.
- Build tool-connected execution environments and formal verification checkers to detect proxy gaming.

## Part Map

- **@sec-architecture-20-ontology (The AI-Assisted Design Life Cycle):** Establishes the stage-gated lifecycle and immutable Operational Attempt Records.
- **@sec-data-representations-world-models (Architecture Data, Knowledge, and Representation):** Classifies hardware graphs (AST, CDFG, SystemC TLM 2.0) and PDK NDA abstractions.
- **@sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization (Prediction, Generation, and Optimization for Architecture Design):** Compares search heuristics, generative models, and physical floorplanning methods.
- **@sec-architecture-environments-tool-interfaces (Tool-Connected Design Environments):** Integrates full-system tools (gem5, VCS, FireSim, OpenROAD, ZeBu, Palladium).
- **@sec-feedback-verification-trust (Verification, Feedback, and Learning):** Constructs formal verification checkers (SVA, UPF PST, RedHawk-SC) to prevent proxy gaming.

## Guiding Questions

1. How do we maintain machine-usable state alignment between learned surrogate models and version-controlled hardware records?
2. What mechanisms prevent AI search algorithms from exploiting unmodeled physical edge cases in fast evaluation proxies?
